verses.sanskrit:
वैशंपायन उवाच।
              कृतास्त्रान्धार्तराष्ट्रांश्च पाण्डुपुत्रांश्च भारत। दृष्ट्वा द्रोणोऽब्रवीद्राजन्धृतराष्ट्रं जनेश्वरम्॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said : O descendant of the Bharata, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra and Pandu expert in arms, O king, Drona thus spoke to the king Dhritarashtra, in the presence of Kripa, Somadatta, Balhika, the wise son of Ganga (Bhishma). Vyasa and Vidura.

verses.sanskrit: कृपस्य सोमदत्तस्य बाह्लीकस्य च धीमतः। गाङ्गेयस्य च सान्निध्ये व्यासस्य विदुरस्य च॥२॥
राजन्संप्राप्तविद्यास्ते कुमाराः कुरुसत्तम। ते दर्शयेयुः स्वां शिक्षां राजन्ननुमते तव॥३॥
verses.english: "O king, O best of the Kurus, your sons have completed their education. Let them with your perinission show their proficiency." Thereupon the great king replied with a delightful heart.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽब्रवीन्महाराजः प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना।
              धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              भारद्वाज महत्कर्म कृतं ते द्विजसत्तम॥४॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said: son will see my O best of Brahmanas, you have accomplished a great deed. O of Bharadvaja, command me yourself as to the place and time, where and when and the manner in which, the trial may be held.

verses.sanskrit: यदानुमन्यसे कालं यस्मिन्देशे यथायथा। तथा तथा विधानाय स्वयमाज्ञापयस्व माम्॥५॥
स्पृहयाम्यद्य निर्वेदान्पुरुषाणां सचक्षुषाम्। अस्त्रहेतोः पराक्रान्तान्ये मे द्रक्ष्यन्ति पुत्रकान्॥६॥
verses.english: Grief for my blindness makes me envy those men who are blessed with sight and who children's prowess in arms.

verses.sanskrit: क्षत्तर्यद्गुरुराचार्यो ब्रवीति कुरु तत्तथा। न हीदृशं प्रियं मन्ये भविता धर्मवत्सल॥७॥
verses.english: O Kshatta (Vidura), do all that the respected preceptor says. O lover of virtue, I think nothing can be more agreeable to me than this.
verses.bhavadeepa: निर्वेदात् दुःखात् सचक्षुषां स्पृहयामि सुखायेति शेषः ॥६॥

verses.sanskrit: ततो राजानमामन्त्र्य निर्गतो विदुरो बहिः। भारद्वाजो महाप्राज्ञो मापयामास मेदिनीम्॥८॥
verses.english: Thereupon Vidura, giving the necessary assurance to the king, went out to do what he was bidden. The greatly learned son of Bharadvaja (Drona) measured a piece of (ground).

verses.sanskrit: समामवृक्षां निर्गुल्मामुदक्प्रस्रवणान्विताम्। तस्यां भूमौ बलिं चक्रे तिथौ नक्षत्रपूजिते॥९॥
verses.english: Which was void of trees and thickets and which was furnished with wells thickets and which was furnished with wells and springs. On this piece of land, that first of eloquent men, that hero (Drona), gave offerings to the gods according to the precepts of the Shastras, when all the people were assembled by proclamation on an auspicious day with an auspicious star in ascendance. O best of men, the artisans built a great auditorium by the order of the king; (they built) another for the (royal) ladies also according to the proper form. The citizens built many platforms and the wealthy men many spacious and high Sibikas.

verses.sanskrit: अवघुष्टे समाजे च तदर्थं वदतां वरः। रङ्गभूमौ सुविपुलं शास्त्रदृष्टं यथाविधि॥१०॥
verses.bhavadeepa: निर्गुल्मां तृणसमूहमूलपिण्डरहिताम् । उदक् प्रस्रवणान्विताम् उदक् निम्नाम् ॥९॥

verses.sanskrit: प्रेक्षागारं सुविहितं चक्रस्ते तस्य शिल्पिनः। रक्षां सर्वायुधोपेतां स्त्रीणां चैव नरर्षभ॥११॥
verses.bhavadeepa: तदर्थं बल्यर्थं समाजे वीरसमूहे अवघुष्टे डिण्डीवशब्देनाहृते सति बलिं चक्रे इति पूर्वेणान्वयः ॥१०॥

verses.sanskrit: मञ्चांश्च कारयामासुर्यत्र जानपदा जनाः। विपुलानुच्छ्रयोपेताशिन् बिकाश्च महाधनाः॥१२॥
verses.bhavadeepa: राज्ञः स्त्रीणां प्रेक्षार्थमागारं मञ्चाश्च इतरेषां प्रेक्षार्थं रङ्गभूमौ चक्रुरिति द्वयोः सम्बन्धः ॥११॥

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिंस्ततोऽहनि प्राप्ते राजा ससचिवस्तदा। भीष्मं प्रमुखतः कृत्वा कृपं चाचार्यसत्तमम्॥१३॥
verses.english: When the (fixed) day came, the king accompanied by his ministers, with Bhishma and Kripa, the excellent preceptor, walking at the head (of the procession). Came to the auditorium of celestial beauty, made of pure gold and decked with strings of pearls and stones of Vaidurya gems.

verses.sanskrit: मुक्ताजालपरिक्षिप्तं वैदूर्यममिशोभितम्। शातकुम्भमयं दिव्यं प्रेक्षागारमुपागमत्॥१४॥
गान्धारी च महाभागा कुन्ती च जयतां वर। स्त्रियश्च राज्ञः सर्वास्ताः सप्रेष्याः सपरिच्छदाः॥१५॥
verses.english: The great fortunate Gandhari and Kunti and the other ladies of the royal household, dressed in gorgeous attire and accompanied by their maids in waiting, joyfully ascended the platforms as celestial ladies ascended the Sumeru mountain. Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and the others of the four orders of caste hurriedly left the city and came running there with the desire of seeing the princes skill in arms and they were so anger that they assembled all there in a moment.

verses.sanskrit: हर्षादारुरुहुर्मञ्चान्मेरुं देवस्त्रियो यथा। ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियाद्यं च चातुर्वर्ण्यं पुराद्द्रुतम्॥१६॥
दर्शनेप्सुः समभ्यागात्कुमाराणां कृतास्त्रताम्। क्षणेनैकस्थतां तत्र दर्शनेप्सुर्जगाम ह॥१७॥
प्रवादितैश्च वादित्रैर्जनकौतूहलेन च। महार्णव इव क्षुब्धः समाजः सोऽभवत्तदा॥१८॥
verses.english: That vast crowd with the noise of blowing trumpets and beating drums and the sounds of many voices became like an agitated ocean.

verses.sanskrit: ततः शुक्लाम्बरधरः शुक्लयज्ञोपवीतवान्। शुक्लकेशः सितश्मश्रुः शुक्लाल्यानुलेपनः॥१९॥
verses.english: Then the preceptor, clad in white attire, with white sacred thread, white locks, white bread, white garlands and white sandal-paste besmeared over his body, entered the arena with his son. It appeared as if the moon accompanied (the planet) Mars appeared in an unclouded sky.

verses.sanskrit: रङ्गमध्यं तदाचार्यः सपुत्रः प्रविवेश ह। नभो जलधरैर्हीनं साङ्गारक इवांशुमान्॥२०॥
स यथा समयं चक्रे बलिं बलवतां वरः। ब्राह्मणांस्तु सुमन्त्रज्ञान्कारयामास मङ्गलम्॥२१॥
verses.english: The best of strong men, the hero (Drona), entering at the proper time, caused Brahmanas versed in Mantras to celebrate the auspicious rites.

verses.sanskrit: सुखपुण्याहघोषस्य पुण्यस्य समनन्तरम्। विविशुर्विविधं गृह्य शस्त्रोपकरणं नराः॥२२॥
verses.english: After auspicious and sweet-sounding musical instruments had struck up as propitiatory ceremony, men equipped with various weapons entered the arena.

verses.sanskrit: ततो बद्धाङ्गुलित्राणा बद्धकक्ष्या महारथाः। बद्धतूणाः सधनुषो विविशुर्भरतर्षभाः॥२३॥
verses.english: Then the best of the Bharata race, (the princes), those mighty car-warriors, having girt up their lions, entered (the arena) equipped with bows, quivers and finger protectors.

verses.sanskrit: अनुज्येष्ठं च ते तत्र युधिष्ठिरपुनरोगमाः। चक्रुरस्त्रं महावीर्याः कुमाराः परमाद्भुतम्॥२४॥
verses.english: With Yudhisthira, at their head, the greatly heroic princes, in the order of their age, began to show wonderful skill in their arms. a
verses.bhavadeepa: बद्धकक्षाः वस्त्रादिना संवृतां सपृष्टोदरा इत्यर्थः । कक्षा बाहुमूलम्  ॥२३॥

verses.sanskrit: केचिच्छराक्षेपभयाच्छिरांस्यवननामिरे। मनुजा धृष्टमपरे वीक्षाञ्चक्रुः सुविस्मिताः॥२५॥
verses.english: Some (spectators) lowered their heads out of fear of the falling arrows, while others not being afraid, looked on with wonder and astonishment.

verses.sanskrit: ते स्म लक्ष्याणि बिभिदुर्बाणैर्नामाङ्कशोभितैः। विविधैर्लाघवोत्सृष्टैरुह्यन्तो वाजिभिर्द्रुतम्॥२६॥
verses.english: Riding swift horses and managing them dextrously, the princess hit marks with arrows engraved with their respective names.

verses.sanskrit: तत्कुमारबलं तत्र गृहीतशरकार्मुकम्। गन्धर्वनगराकारं प्रेक्ष्य ते विस्मिताऽभवन्॥२७॥
verses.english: On seeing the prowess of the princes in using bows and arrows, the spectators thought they were seeing the city of Gandharva. They were all filled with amazement.

verses.sanskrit: सहसा चुक्रुशुश्चान्ये नराः शतसहस्रशः। विस्मयोत्फुल्लनयनाः साधु साध्विति भारत॥२८॥
verses.english: O descendant of Bharata, some hundreds and thousands of men, their eyes expanded with wonder, all at once cried out “Well done! Well done!"

verses.sanskrit: कृत्वा धनुषि ते मार्गान्रथचर्यासु चासकृत्। गजपृष्ठेऽश्वपृष्ठे च नियुद्धे च महाबलाः॥२९॥
verses.english: After repeatedly displaying their skill and dexterity in the use of bow and arrows, in the management of cars, in the fight on horseback and on the back of elephants.

verses.sanskrit: गृहीतखड्गचर्माणस्ततो भूयः प्रहारिणः। त्सरुमार्गान्यथोद्दिष्टांश्चेरुः सर्वासु भूमिषु॥३०॥
verses.english: They took up their swords and buckles and began to attack one another and to walk around the arena displaying various modes of sword's play.
verses.bhavadeepa: धनुषि मार्गान् तिर्यगूर्ध्वान् चललक्ष्यपातनादीन् । रथचर्यासु मार्गान् शीघ्रंगतप्रत्यागतप्रदक्षिणा प्रदक्षिणमण्डलगत्यादिरूपान् ॥२९॥

verses.sanskrit: लाघवं सौष्ठवं शोभां स्थिरत्वं दृढमुष्टिताम्। ददृशुस्तत्र सर्वेषां प्रयोगं खड्गचर्मणोः॥३१॥
verses.english: They all saw their (great) agility, the beauty of the symmetry of their bodies, their grace, their calmness, the firmness of their grasp and the skill in the use of their swords and buckles.
verses.bhavadeepa: त्सरुमार्गान् तिर्यगूर्ध्वाधःखङ्गप्रचलनरूपान् । सर्वासु भूमिषु रथादिपृष्ठेषु भुवि वा ॥३०॥

verses.sanskrit: अथ तौ नित्यसंहृष्टौ सुयोधनवृकोदरौ। अवतीर्णौ गदाहस्तावेकशृङ्गाविवाचलौ॥३२॥
verses.english: Then Vrikodara (Bhima) and Suyodhana (Duryodhana) entered the (arena)with secret mental delight like two single peaked mountains.
verses.bhavadeepa: लाघवं शैघ्र्यं सौष्ठवं चातुरीम् । एकेनैव खड्गेन समन्ताद्भ्रामितेन युगपदनेकायुधनिवारणम् । शोभां सर्वतो झलझलायमानैकखङ्गांशुमण्डलान्तरगतत्वेनाभिनवाम् । स्थिरत्वमभीतत्वम् । दृढमुष्टितां खङ्गभृतां हस्त एव परितश्चलति न त्वङ्गुल्य इत्यर्थः । प्रयोगं निदर्शनम् ॥३१॥

verses.sanskrit: बद्धकक्ष्यौ महाबाहू पौरुषे पर्यवस्थितौ। बृंहन्तौ वासिताहेतोः समदाविव कुञ्जरौ॥३३॥
verses.english: Those mighty-armed heroes girt their lions and summoned all their strength; they roared like two infuriated elephants contending (for a female elephant).

verses.sanskrit: तौ प्रदक्षिणसव्यानि मण्डलानि महाबलौ। चेरतुर्मण्डलगतौ समदाविव कुञ्जरौ॥३४॥
verses.english: Those two greatly strong (heroes) circled round the arena with faultless clubs and careered right and left in all the proper form.

verses.sanskrit: विदुरो धृतराष्ट्राय गान्धार्याः पाण्डवारणिः। न्यवेदयेतां तत्सर्वं कुमाराणां विचेष्टितम्॥३५॥
verses.english: Vidura described to Dhritarashtra and the mother of the Pandavas (Kunti) to Gandhari all the feats of the princes.
verses.bhavadeepa: चेरतुः पद्भ्याम् । मण्डलगतौ अलातचक्रवद्भ्राम्यमाणगदापरिवेषान्तर्गतौ । निर्मलगदाविति पाठे स्पष्टोऽर्थः ॥३४॥
